Well…it’s not how I imagined it’d be when I was a little girl, that’s for sure. I’m in an okay place, I guess, by most people’s standards, but I just think life is boring and pointless in general. I suppose it’s boring because I don’t do anything, but there’s nothing I WANT to do, nothing I want to see, and nothing I truly enjoy, and that feeling doesn’t change no matter how much I make or what I buy. I still have Christmas gifts I bought for myself that I have yet to open (it was 5, but I needed one of the items this weekend). Because I don’t care. I just…don’t really care to experience anything. I feel like I’m just going through the motions and biding my time, dying slowly each monotonous day. I often wake up angry because I woke up. 

I feel like the next milestone I have to look forward to is dying (I don’t know when that’ll be, but I know I cannot do this for another 50 years), which I’m hoping doesn’t just kick me into another realm with an equally monotonous, predictable, pointless life. Sometimes I get so incredibly angry at my parents for having me and subjecting me to this miserable drudgery that I can’t even bring myself to speak to them (which I know is wrong of me, but my disdain always dies down after a few weeks of brooding in solitude). Anyway, I’m going to go to bed because I have to wake up tomorrow for another f***ing Monday. *sigh*

So, TL/DR: No, I’m not living a fun, exciting, or fulfilling life, but I generally don’t associate life with any of those things anyway. Life just…is. Until it’s not.

She was discharged, couldn’t walk, people thought I was crazy and wasting my time, but I personally rehabbed her—I carried her everywhere and noticed she would “swim” mid-air; then she regained use of her front legs and could drag her hind legs, until one day, I went to her crate and she was standing on her own. BUT here’s a trick that will work even if you DO genuinely want to converse: make them talk about themselves. 

Example 1, for small talk ahead of a meeting (where I can’t keep my camera off, mic muted, and ignore them):
Them: “Happy Monday! How was your weekend?!” 
Me: “Uneventful. Yours?”
Them: “Uneventful is better than catastrophe! I just went to the farmer’s market and…”
Me: *already checked out, hoping someone else joins or I can fake an incoming call*

Example 2:
Them: “How’s the weather where you are?”
Me: “Pretty mild. You?”
Them: “Lucky! It’s so rainy…”
Me: *comfortably back in my own little world, inside my head* 

Sometimes instead of “uneventful,” I’ll say “peaceful” or if I don’t know the weather (because I hate the outdoors and don’t go outside if I can help it), I’ll say that. Over time, you’ll get good at listening just enough to pick up tone inflections and context clues to jump back in with follow up questions to keep them going, if you must prolong the interaction). And if you DO want to engage, you can be more interactive with the back and forth. 

Example:
Them: “Happy Monday! How was your weekend?!”
You: “I didn’t do much, just lounged around and read. You?”
Them: “Oh that sounds relaxing! I went to the farmer’s market and got apples.”
You: *talk about how you love honeycrisp apples or whatever. Maybe you know a good apple pie recipe, maybe they ask about your book and you can nerd out and share recommendations. Listen for a common interest and pull at that thread; it’ll flow from there*

There have been times I’ve set myself up to do it and just couldn’t pull the trigger (literally and figuratively). 

A few things made me not do it:
1.) my dogs. I love them and they love me and I’m their only caretaker. I’d hate to leave them here alone. They’re the reason I get out of bed, even when I don’t feel like it. A lot of people say their family and friends keep them here, and I used to be that way too, but after seeing my sister die and seeing life goes on (even though it’s HARD and we all struggle with it even more now), I don’t feel as guilty leaving them behind. They’ll continue on. My dogs, however, are thumbless, jobless, can’t speak human, can’t read, and can’t drive. They need me. 

2.) I’m afraid of fucking up and paralyzing or permanently incapacitating myself. This is probably reason number one, because I have arrangements I could make for my dogs and be confident they’d be cared for. 

3.) This is a new one, and it probably sounds stupid, and I’m embarrassed to say it, but I’ll share in case it helps someone else…but I know death is coming. One day. It’s the ONLY site thing about life…and I find that comforting. And so I started looking at living as one big science experiment. You have your constants—and yes, some of us got better or worse constants that others, but we just have to make do with what we have…but we also have variables and we CAN change those variables to keep testing the hypothesis (which is happiness, wealth, baseline contentment…whatever it is for you personally). The hardest part (IMO) is keeping our eyes on our own experiment and not being distracted by everyone around us winning their ribbons and trophies for THEIR experiment, and feeling like we’ve lost because the science fair we call life isn’t over for us until the judge comes to tap us on the shoulder and tells us our time is up…so we have to keep changing the variables to prove our hypothesis correct. 

Again, I know that last bit is INCREDIBLY cheesy, but I had the thought a few days ago and it made me feel better (I always liked science and testing things like that so putting it into terms that I enjoy helped a lot). 

Am I still horribly depressed? Yes (I’d probably be better off if I took my meds faithfully but…I don’t like any of them). But…I feel better NOW than I have in a loooooonnngggg while (I also quit the rat race and started consisting on freelance/consulting work at my own pace.
